LLM auditresponse for runtime-sync:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a routine runtime helper script that synchronizes the package's read-only installation directory (`/usr/lib/zotero-pdf2zh`) into a writable runtime location (`/var/lib/zotero-pdf2zh/app`) before execution. It uses `rsync` with `--delete` to mirror files, but carefully excludes user configuration files (`config.json`, `config.toml`, `venv.json`, `package_update_state.json`), virtual environments (`zotero-pdf2zh*-venv*`), the `translated/` output directory, and `__pycache__/`. This is standard packaging practice: it keeps read-only `/usr/lib` pristine while allowing persistent runtime state (configs, translations, Python environments) in `/var/lib`, which survives package upgrades.

I checked for the typical threat patterns: there are no network requests, no downloads from any host, no `curl`/`wget`/`eval`/`base64` usage, no obfuscation or encoding tricks, and no exfiltration of local data. The script only operates on its own application's installed path and a private `/var/lib` directory it manages. The `--delete` flag is constrained to the destination it populates, and nothing outside the app's scope is touched.

This is the kind of benign maintainer/runtime script that is normal in AUR packages (especially for Python/uv-based apps with read-only file hierarchies). No supply-chain attack indicators present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard rsync helper copying installed files to writable runtime dir. No security issues.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
